title: Third-party vs. native harness: muse-spark-1.3 on Pi vs. Muse Code
subtitle: Same Meta model — Pi beat the native harness on every metric.
description: A 7-slide controlled harness ablation of Meta's muse-spark-1.3-contributor (#high) on Pi vs. Muse Code: how Pi hit 7/7 for $0.14 while Muse Code's Seatbelt sandbox, 8.5× larger prompt, and Turn-339 compaction stalled at 6/7.

slides.label: COVER
slides.headlinePrimary: When a third-party harness beats the native one.
slides.headlineMuted: muse-spark-1.3 on Pi vs. Muse Code.
slides.lead: Exact same Meta weights and `#high` effort — **Pi** passed **7/7** for **$0.14**, while **Muse Code** stalled at **6/7**.

slides.label: PROMPT & CONTEXT TAX
slides.headlinePrimary: An 8.5× bigger system prompt compounded fast.
slides.headlineMuted: Muse Code burned 74.07M tokens — #1 highest on the board.

slides.headlinePrimary: Faster, half the tokens, and a full pass.

slides.label: CASE STUDY #1 SANDBOX BLIND SPOT
slides.headlinePrimary: Muse Code's sandbox hid 16 failing tests.
slides.headlineMuted: And blinded the agent on S7 Ctrl-C.

steps.title: Seatbelt blocked loopback & PTYs
steps.desc: Muse Code's `proxy_only` sandbox rejected loopback TCP (`:eperm`) and blocked real PTY allocation during agent test runs.

steps.title: Wrong S7 diagnosis
steps.desc: Without a real foreground terminal, the model misdiagnosed background `&` `SIG_IGN` and port process-group isolation.

steps.title: 16 failures on the real host
steps.desc: Running `mix test` outside the sandbox exposed **81/97** tests passing and a broken `S7` foreground `Ctrl-C` handler.

callout.title: Harness Sandbox ≠ Reality
callout.body: A strict sandbox can prevent an agent from verifying networking and PTY code — turning a capable model into a **6/7** run.

slides.label: CASE STUDY #2 HOW PI WON S7
slides.headlinePrimary: Unblocked on Pi, the same model solved S7.

steps.title: Zero-dep HTTP/1.1 + TLS (`deps: []`)
steps.desc: Hand-rolled a streaming HTTP/1.1 + TLS client in S3 while solving Mix's `:ssl` code-path pruning and `:logger_std_h` stderr routing.

steps.title: 15.7-minute S7 signal root-cause
steps.desc: With real PTY access on Pi, it uncovered OTP's `:erl_signal_handler` race against `System.trap_signal(:sigterm, ...)` and fixed it cleanly.

steps.title: No context compaction needed
steps.desc: Peak context stayed at **254.1k** across 262 turns, avoiding the mid-turn compaction drift that hit Muse Code at Turn 339.

callout.title: Cheapest Paid 7/7 on the Board
callout.body: At **$0.14** (`99.28%` cache hit), Pi + `muse-spark-1.3` beat every other paid 7/7 run by nearly **10×**.

slides.label: FIELD NOTES
slides.headlinePrimary: Pi won the run, not every detail.

items.head: Pi skipped Credo (9 post-run issues)
items.text: Pi left `deps: []` with no linter, whereas Muse Code built a custom AST lint gate (`mix capy_bench.lint`).

items.head: Turn-339 compaction amnesia on Muse Code
items.text: Mid-turn async compaction at **384k** tokens caused Muse Code's final summary to claim S1–S7 were 'already implemented'.

items.head: Silent crash dumps & pipe-masked errors
items.text: On Pi, only 3 of 179 bash calls flagged `isError: true` because pipes masked red-phase failures and 4 silent `erl_crash.dump` files.

items.head: Ultra-cheap cache pricing hid token bloat
items.text: A **98% cache discount** (`$0.002/1M`) kept 74.07M tokens at `$0.25` — at standard flash rates, that volume would cost **$2.40+**.

slides.label: TAKEAWAYS & ARCHIVE
slides.headlinePrimary: 3 lessons from Pi vs. Muse Code.
slides.headlineMuted: Never judge a model by one harness.

items.head: The native harness isn't always best
items.text: Third-party **Pi** beat native **Muse Code** on pass rate (`7/7` vs `6/7`), speed (`-27%`), tokens (`-49%`), and cost (`-44%`).

items.head: Lean prompts protect long-horizon work
items.text: Starting at `3.4k` instead of `29.2k` tokens avoided a `384k` mid-turn compaction that broke end-of-run coherence.

items.head: Sandboxes must match target runtime
items.text: Blocking loopback TCP and PTYs makes network and CLI benchmarks untestable — masking failures until host verification.
